name: Login Form for Elementor
author: Khawaja Awais

sections.description:
Login Form for Elementor replaces WordPress’s plain default login page with a custom login widget you can build entirely inside Elementor. Drag it onto any page, style it to match your brand, and give visitors a login experience that actually looks like the rest of your site.

Whether you’re building a membership site, a client portal, a WooCommerce store, or just want your login page to stop looking like it’s from 2003 — this widget gives you full control without touching a line of code.

Why you’ll like it

  • 🎨 Looks like your site, not WordPress core. Style every element — fields, button, labels, links — right from the Elementor panel.
  • ⚡ Set up in under a minute. Drag the widget in, it just works. No shortcodes, no settings pages to hunt through.
  • 🔒 Clear, specific error messages. Users are told exactly whether their username or password was wrong — less support tickets, better UX.
  • 🧩 Built for Elementor, properly. Native controls, typography panels, and Global Colors support — it behaves like a first-party Elementor widget.
  • 🛠️ Granular styling control, right down to input border radius, field typography, and font weights.

Features

Content controls
* Custom form title
* Editable labels for Username and Password (or hide them entirely)
* Editable placeholder text for both fields
* Toggle “Remember Me” checkbox on/off
* Custom button text

Style controls
* Button background & text color (with Elementor Global Colors support)
* Button border radius
* Input field border color, width, and radius
* Forgot-password link color
* Independent typography controls for input fields, the Remember Me label, and the Forgot Password link — font family, size, and weight, all separately adjustable

Perfect for

  • Membership and subscription sites
  • Client portals and dashboards
  • WooCommerce “My Account” style login pages
  • Any site where the default wp-login.php page just doesn’t fit the brand
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it directly from your WordPress dashboard via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate Login Form for Elementor through the Plugins menu.
  3. Edit any page with Elementor and search for “Custom Login Form” in the widget panel.
  4. Drag it onto your page, then use the Content and Style tabs to make it your own.

That’s it — no configuration screens, no extra setup.
sections.faq:
How do I add the custom login form to my site?

Edit a page with Elementor and drag the “Custom Login Form” widget onto your layout from the widgets panel. It’s fully functional the moment you drop it in.

Can I customize the labels, placeholders, and button text?

Yes — every piece of text on the form (title, labels, placeholders, button text) is editable from the Content tab, no code needed.

Can I style it to match my site’s branding?

Yes. Colors, border radius, border width, and typography for each part of the form are all controllable from the Style tab, including support for Elementor Global Colors.

Does this replace the default WordPress login page?

No — it adds a login widget you can place on any Elementor page. Your default wp-login.php still works as normal alongside it.

Will it work with my theme?

Since the form is built and styled entirely inside Elementor, it works independently of your active theme’s styling.

What happens if a user enters the wrong password?

They’ll see a clear, specific error message telling them whether the issue was the username or the password, instead of a generic failure message.
